text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Hamas spokesman welcomes Jordan's efforts to get former Hamas political chief Abu Marzook released from New York jail and returned to Jordan.
- Government urged to follow up rights of Jordanians who own property on the West Bank.
- Germany's Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel to visit Jordan in March.
- Deputy Head of Central Bank Marto says Jordan to receive $40 million from World Bank on Tuesday, the first instalment of $340 million loan to bolster reserves and support economic reforms.
- Information Minister Marwan Muasher says Jordan is committed to getting a just settlement for Jordanian-owned "absentee property" in Israel.
- King Hussein in Bonn today for talks with Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
- Crown Prince Hassan meets Congolese minister of state for transport and civil aviation.
- Central Bank's Marto says Jordan's foreign reserves will reach $800 million after it gets World Bank loans.
- Public Works Minister Abdul-Hadi al-Majali warns engineers that strikes will not help them.
- Twenty-one Jordanian companies have received ISO-9000 certificates, another 60 expecting to receive them.
- Iraqi Minister of Trade Saleh on a secret visit to Amman.
- Iraqi Minister of Trade Mohammed Mehdi Saleh discusses trade ties with Minister of Trade and Industry Ali Abu al-Ragheb.
- No tangible results yet from efforts to free Jordanian priosners in Kuwait.
- Congolese President Pascal Lissouba to visit Jordan.
